title: POC Decision Matrix: Facilitator Brief and Slide Skeleton
content:
Purpose:
This facilitator brief is designed to run a compact, decision-oriented POC workshop with customer stakeholders. The objective is to surface trade-offs, align on success criteria, and produce a clear go/no-go recommendation by the end of the session. Use this when we need to de-risk deployment decisions (model variant, latency targets, capacity tier) and capture an explicit decision matrix that the customer can attach to their evaluation artifacts.

Audience and roles (recommended):
- Customer executive sponsor (business outcome owner) — 30m availability
- Customer engineering lead — hands-on, owns integration questions
- Customer SRE/security representative — asks infra and compliance questions
- Solutions engineering facilitator (you) — runs the session
- SE subject-matter experts (runtime, infra) — available for clarifying questions (on-call)

Pre-reqs (to collect 3 days before):
- Short pre-read: current architecture diagram, example traffic profile (p50/p90 seq length), target latency SLA
- Baseline evaluation artifacts: sample prompts and example outputs from candidate model(s) if available
- Contact list with decision authority and proxy decision-makers
- Confirm environment constraints (VPC, KMS, on-prem options)

Logistics:
- Duration: 120 minutes (recommended)
- Format: hybrid (Zoom + Miro board for decision matrix)
- Materials to prepare: slide deck skeleton, blank decision matrix template (CSV/Miro), scoring rubric handout, follow-up tasks sheet

Workshop agenda (timeboxed):
1) 00:00–00:10 — Kickoff and alignment
  - Quick intros (name + decision area)
  - Workshop objective and expected outcomes (explicit: decision matrix + next steps)
2) 00:10–00:25 — Problem & constraints recap (customer speaks)
  - Ask customer lead to describe top-3 goals for the POC and non-negotiable constraints
  - Clarify performance targets, regulatory constraints, and integration must-haves
3) 00:25–00:45 — Candidate solutions overview (SE gives a focused briefing)
  - 3 candidate paths (Host API, Dedicated reserved pool, Private deploy) or model variants (quantized, fp16, distilled)
  - Show quick cost/latency heuristics per path (use real numbers or ranges)
4) 00:45–01:15 — Build the Decision Matrix (guided)
  - Columns: Candidate options (3–4)
  - Rows: Weighted criteria (Latency, Cost, Implementation Effort, Reliability, Data Isolation, Supportability, Maturity)
  - Use rubric: 1–5 for each criterion, multiply by weight; capture comments for each cell
  - Facilitator action: call on specific participants to score rows to avoid groupthink
5) 01:15–01:35 — Scenario walk-through and sensitivity checks
  - Run 2 short scenarios (peak traffic burst, regulatory audit) and ask: which candidate survives?
  - Adjust weights if scenario priorities change
6) 01:35–01:50 — Risk register and mitigations
  - Rapidly capture top 5 risks per leading candidate and assign owners
7) 01:50–02:00 — Decision capture, next steps, close
  - Record final scores and a clear recommendation (go with X, pilot Y, or proof-of-concept extension)
  - Agree on immediate next actions and primary contact for the pilot

Slide skeleton (10–12 slides) and speaker notes:
- Slide 1: Title + objective + attendees (speaker note: call out decision authority at start)
- Slide 2: One-line problem statement and desired business outcome (speaker note: solicit 1 clarifying sentence from customer)
- Slide 3: Constraints and must-haves (speaker note: prioritize non-negotiables in bold)
- Slide 4: Candidate solution summary (table with 3 columns: path, pros, cons)
- Slide 5: Cost/latency heuristics (graph or bullet ranges; speaker note: be explicit about assumptions)
- Slide 6: Decision matrix template (blank) — move to Miro for live scoring
- Slide 7: Scoring rubric and weights (show how to calculate)
- Slide 8: Scenario outcomes (2 quick cases)
- Slide 9: Top risks and mitigations (speaker note: capture owners live)
- Slide 10: Recommendation and rationale (speaker note: include numeric results and qualitative notes)
- Slide 11: Next steps, owners, and timeline (speaker note: set calendar dates before closing)
- Slide 12: Appendix (metrics definitions, sample prompts, evaluation caveats)

Facilitation cues and tips:
- Avoid paralysis by analysis: if a row is disputed, ask for the proxy decision-maker’s input; move on after 90 seconds of discussion
- Use a visible timer for each agenda block to keep momentum
- Balance quantitative scores with short qualitative comments — those comments are what the exec sponsor reads later
- When a participant rates a candidate very low, always ask for a short justification (prevents hidden assumptions)
- If group converges too quickly, run a sensitivity test: change the weight of one critical row by +50% and re-run totals to show fragility

Scoring rubric (suggested weights):
- Latency: 25%
- Cost per token / hour: 20%
- Implementation effort (weeks): 15%
- Reliability / SLA fit: 15%
- Data isolation & compliance: 15%
- Supportability / vendor maturity: 10%
Note: weights must sum to 100; adjust per-customer priorities before the workshop.

Common objections and suggested responses:
- "We can’t accept managed data processing": show Private deployment and VPC/KMS options, and pull a short compliance checklist from appendix
- "Latency targets are too strict": propose a canary with dedicated pool + fallback to hosted API for bursts
- "Cost looks high": demonstrate unit economics from Redwood Optimize (batching, quantization) and outline savings levers in the pilot

Outputs to deliver within 48 hours post-workshop:
- Finalized decision matrix CSV with scores and comments (owner: SE facilitator)
- Short one-page recommendation memo signed by customer sponsor (owner: customer sponsor)
- Action tracker with owners, dates, and gating criteria (owner: SE facilitator)
- Optional: pilot-run checklist for the chosen candidate (owner: assigned SE)

Follow-up checklist for facilitator (quick):
- Upload filled matrix to customer Confluence page + attach to POC ticket
- Create follow-up calendar invites for pilot kickoff and technical deep-dive
- Share slide PDF and rubric handout with all attendees
- Add risks to customer’s shared risk register and assign owners

Notes to SEs prepping the session:
- Precompute one sample scoring across candidates so you can show a worked example during the 'build matrix' segment — helps participants understand the math
- Prepare one demo snippet (if applicable) that shows an observable difference (latency or output quality) between candidates
- Keep the discussion customer-centric: translate technical trade-offs back to business outcomes (time-to-market, cost per active user, compliance risk)

Appendix (quick references):
- Short definitions: what we mean by "implementation effort" (integration + infra + validation)
- Link to Redwood Dedicated SLA summary (insert URL in linked_artifacts)

End of brief.

Facilitator contact: sophia.nguyen@redwood.ai
